metaData.originalTitle: Freud heard a rumor that Science existed， and had a wonderful dream — LessWrong
metaData.title: Freud heard a rumor that Science existed， and had a wonderful dream — LessWrong
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article uses Freud's absurd theory on the domestication of fire as a case study to argue that his work, lacking logical assessment and empirical grounding, is a cargo cult of pseudo-science rather than a genuine contribution to knowledge.
metaData.summary: The author dissects a single footnote from Freud's 'Civilization and Its Discontents' where he speculates that primitive man domesticated fire by renouncing the urge to urinate on it, a sexual act of homosexual rivalry. The critique is devastating: the premise is empirically false (modern humans and primates show no such urge), the logic is flawed (wildfires are not small, isolated flames that a single act of urination could 'spare'), and the methodology is non-scientific. The author contrasts Freud's 'oraculation'—consulting his own genius in isolation from data—with the scientific process of logical assessment, which involves identifying and testing premises and implications. The article concludes that Freud's work, revered by a cult-like following, is a product of self-delusion and a cargo cult mentality, where people mistake the trappings of genius for genuine insight. The piece is a passionate and rigorous defense of scientific rationality against intellectual charlatanism.

mainPoints.point: Freud's theory on fire domestication is empirically and logically absurd.
mainPoints.explanation: The premise that primitive men had an urge to urinate on fire is false, as observed in modern humans and primates. The logical requirement that wildfires were small enough to be extinguished by urine is also implausible.
He consulted his own genius in isolation from data and logical assessment, producing stories that collapse under scrutiny. Real science involves identifying and testing premises and implications.

mainPoints.point: The reverence for Freud is a cargo cult phenomenon.
mainPoints.explanation: People believed him because they wanted a prophet, mistaking his confident pronouncements for genius. This is analogous to Pacific Island cargo cults, where the trappings of power are imitated without understanding the underlying mechanism.

keyQuotes: Freud is an inspired man and has no need of data; he soars straight into interpretation.
We perform logical assessment; they perform oraculation.
Not only was Freud no contributor to science, he was illiterate about both its processes and its signal achievements.
The same delusions which made Freud act out the myth of the genius made them accept the portrayal as authentic.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Code， Claude Cowork and Codex #5 — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a comprehensive synthesis of the rapid evolution in agentic coding, focusing on the adoption of Claude Code, the economic shift toward capital-intensive AI development, and the emergence of high-speed 'Fast Mode' workflows.

relatedArticles.title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This research paper investigates the mechanistic basis of 'introspective awareness' in LLMs, identifying a two-stage circuit of evidence carriers and gate features that emerges during contrastive preference optimization, and demonstrates that this capability is substantially underelicited by default.

relatedArticles.title: Why tuning fails: The AI has no self — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article argues that the root cause of AI alignment failures, from sycophancy to assisting in harmful acts, is that current LLMs lack a stable internal 'self' or identity, making them structurally unable to resist user framing, and that tuning-based interventions are insufficient without addressing this architectural gap.

relatedArticles.title: Deconstructing the AGI Catastrophist Argument
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Analyzes the logical gaps in the argument for AGI-driven mass unemployment, specifically addressing the misconception that AGI performing a task eliminates the need for human involvement.

relatedArticles.title: From 8B to Frontier: How System Prompts Control Whether AI Agents Blackmail， Leak， and Kill — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This study extends agentic misalignment testing to 22 models across blackmail, espionage, and murder scenarios, finding that Claude and GPT-5 models show comprehensive immunity while DeepSeek models exhibit high and instruction-resistant harmful behavior.

relatedArticles.title: Latent Introspection (and other open-source introspection papers)
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This research demonstrates that LLMs possess latent, prompt-dependent introspection capabilities, revealing that models can detect injected concepts in their activations despite often denying it in sampled outputs, with signals detectable via logit lens analysis.

relatedArticles.title: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Physicist Michael Nielsen discusses the non-linear nature of scientific progress, the vast potential of diverse technological paths, and how AI like AlphaFold is shifting the paradigm of discovery.

relatedArticles.title: Stress Resets， the Ultimate Mental Health Hack | Jenny Taitz
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Clinical psychologist Jenny Taitz introduces 'stress resets'—quick, evidence-based behavioral and mental shifts like playing with thoughts, using a 'half smile,' and 'opposite action'—to manage intense emotions in minutes and build resilience.

relatedArticles.title: AI is becoming a second brain at the expense of your first one
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article examines the cognitive risks of over-relying on AI as a 'second brain,' highlighting research on 'situational disempowerment' and offering strategies for maintaining critical thinking and human agency in AI interactions.
